note: Pairings a person has read and signed (docs/hadith-policy.md §1): a compilation's hadith that is plainly in the book its compiler names, where the measure in build-compilation.js falls short because he words one narration and the book holds another. Each entry: his number, the book, the row's place in the pack (and the number the pack gives it), words the row must hold, who decided and when. Kept short on purpose. A signature never goes outside the compiler's attribution or to a row the app does not serve; the builder refuses one that does.

holds: فمن كانت هجرته إلى الله ورسوله فهجرته إلى الله ورسوله
riyad.why: "Actions are by intentions", from ʿUmar: an-Nawawī calls it agreed upon and gives a wording that is in neither Ṣaḥīḥ word for word (0.79 of this row, under the 0.85 asked). This is al-Bukhārī's narration in the Book of Oaths and Vows — no. 6689 in the numbering of Fatḥ al-Bārī, 6195 in the edition the pack follows — which has both halves of the hadith.
